expected.text: Approving, rejecting and editing claims in the shared memory is done through chat (Slack/Teams), not by exposing git pull requests to reviewers; git, if used at all, is only a hidden storage detail.
expected.evidence: I wouldn't expose the interface of git (pull request) as the primary mechanism when it comes to approving/rejecting/modifying claims about the enterprise in the hive mind.  chat generally is the tool used by agents and humans to communicate.

expected.text: The shared memory starts on a relational Postgres database (not a graph DB or git-backed store) because the agents need fast queries against the shared mind.
expected.evidence: If we can start with a relational DB like Postgres, then that's fine.  We need speed when it comes to the shared mind that the agents need to query from.

expected.text: Memory governance is split by provenance: facts read from a source of truth need no review, while human or bot recollections (lessons, decisions) always go to a reviewer, a central curator on day one.
expected.evidence: I think that split makes sense.

acceptable.text: Deployment of generated artifacts goes through a pluggable DeployTarget seam (Cloud Run first) because the organisation is on Google Cloud but must be able to configure how things deploy rather than assume one platform.
acceptable.evidence: I want to make sure that the system has the seam necessary to configure 'how things get deployed automatically' rather than just assume we have one solution.

acceptable.text: The shared memory serves both non-engineers who describe what they want built and engineers whose bots need to know the estate; these are not treated as alternative first users.
acceptable.evidence: I don't think you have to exclude one case or the other.  I would say both.
